name: Bissau
subtitle: Bissau, capital of Guinea-Bissau: its numbers, a short history and places to see beyond the World Heritage list.

parts.text: Work on building the Fortaleza de São José de Bissau began in 1765, a first step in creating a differentiated space on the island of Bissau.
Only after the Bissau War of 1844 did the Portuguese obtain exclusive control of a small plot of land on the island, a real Portuguese enclave in the territory of the Papel people.
Bissau was founded as a fort in 1765 and, after the slave trade declined in the early 19th century, became the chief commercial centre of Portuguese Guinea.
On 19 December 1941 the capital of Portuguese Guinea was moved from Bolama to Bissau, where new infrastructure including a port had begun to be built.
The Sector Autónomo de Bissau is the Guinea-Bissau administrative unit alongside the eight regions.
In the 2009 census the largest share of the national population, 25.1 percent, lived in the Sector Autónomo de Bissau.
In the Sector Autónomo de Bissau the Balanta (20.5%), Fula (18.0%), Papel (15.7%) and Mandinga peoples were the most numerous ethnic groups in 2009.
For a decade after independence, residents and business owners in Bissau Velho were required by law to repaint their building facades each December.
Bandim, in Bissau, is considered the largest and best-supplied market in the country.

parts.text: 387,909 in 2009, according to the figures compiled from the national statistics office. Which area is counted matters: Sector Autónomo de Bissau (SAB), 3rd General Population and Housing Census 2009 (RGPH-2009), population corrected for post-census survey omission, including collective residents.

items.text: From the arrival of the Portuguese in the region in 1460, Portuguese and Papel peoples contended for power over the social spaces of the island of Bissau.
Construction of the Fortaleza de São José de Bissau began in 1765.
The Bissau War of 1844 allowed the Portuguese to build a real enclave on the island.
Bolama became capital of the Portuguese colony on 18 March 1879, administered separately from Cape Verde.
The colonial capital was transferred from Bolama to Bissau on 19 December 1941.
Guinea-Bissau became independent in 1974; for a decade afterwards Bissau Velho owners had to repaint facades each December.
The 2009 census corrected population of the Sector Autónomo de Bissau was 387,909.
The Bijagós Archipelago – Omatí Minhô became Guinea-Bissau's first World Heritage site.
